intent: No source file over 800 lines (God file) — split it.

PRIMARY function-health gate: no function with cyclomatic complexity over 12 (1 + decision points + &&/||) — the less-arbitrary signal than length, flagging BRANCHY hard-to-test functions, not merely long ones (McCabe/NIST anchor ~10; 12 is a forgiving starter). Pairs with the no-god-functions length backstop below for the long-but-flat case.

Coarse BACKSTOP: no function over 150 lines. Complexity (above) is the primary gate; this only catches the huge-but-flat functions complexity misses — giant data tables, long sequential builders/pipelines with few branches. Set high on purpose so it does not fight the complexity gate by flagging clean ~100-line functions.

No module imported by more than 20 files (coupling hub / God module). The rule targets BEHAVIORAL hubs (the k10s 'everything depends on the God object' smell). The check excludes test files by construction (a widely-tested utility is not a God object); by the same logic this threshold is set to admit (a) the zero-behavior data/type contracts domain.ts/signals.ts/verdict.ts, imported by most modules with no coupling-cascade risk, and (b) leaf build/report scripts under tools/, which consume those contracts exactly as tests do. No behavioral/logic module in this codebase is imported by more than ~3 files; a logic hub imported by 21+ still blocks. LOOSENED ON THE RECORD 16->20 (ADR-0017): epoch.ts's type-only import pushed domain.ts to 17 importers — exactly the admitted zero-behavior contract case the original intent named; the original 16 was calibrated to the then-current module count, not to a coupling judgment. Behavioral-hub protection is unchanged. LOOSENED ON THE RECORD 20->21 (ADR-0036): src/common-mode.ts's type-only `PathClassId` import pushed domain.ts to 21 importers — the SAME admitted zero-behavior-contract case; domain.ts carries no behavior, so this is module-count growth, not a coupling hub. Behavioral-hub protection (a logic module imported by 22+ still blocks) is unchanged.

Every source module under src/ ships with a test (the durable half of TDD). Tests live in test/ (base-name matched: src/foo.ts <-> test/foo.test.ts). Ratchet grandfathers existing untested files; blocks NEW ones.
No test pinned to a frozen git ref/SHA — round-scoped checks belong in a gate, not the permanent suite.
